ready1_open_rewrite.title: SciVerse open question
ready1_open_rewrite.rewritten_question_text: Ammonia and nitrous oxide undergo the following reaction: $$2\mathrm{NH_3(g)} + 3\mathrm{N_2O(g)} \rightarrow 4\mathrm{N_2(g)} + 3\mathrm{H_2O(g)}$$ The enthalpy values of various bonds are known: the $\mathrm{N-H}$ bond enthalpy is $388\mathrm{kJ/mol}$; the $\mathrm{N-O}$ bond enthalpy is $210\mathrm{kJ/mol}$; the $\mathrm{N=O}$ bond enthalpy is $630\mathrm{kJ/mol}$; the $\mathrm{N=N}$ bond enthalpy is $409\mathrm{kJ/mol}$; the $\mathrm{N\equiv N}$ bond enthalpy is $941\mathrm{kJ/mol}$; the $\mathrm{O-H}$ bond enthalpy is $463\mathrm{kJ/mol}$. (1) According to the absolute entropy value chart, calculate the total entropy change of this reaction ($\mathrm{J/mol\cdot K}$); (2) Calculate the total enthalpy change of this reaction ($\mathrm{kJ/mol}$).

ready2_open_rewrite.resolved_question_text: Ammonia and nitrous oxide undergo the following reaction: $$2\mathrm{NH_3(g)} + 3\mathrm{N_2O(g)} \rightarrow 4\mathrm{N_2(g)} + 3\mathrm{H_2O(g)}$$ The enthalpy values of various bonds are known: the $\mathrm{N-H}$ bond enthalpy is $388\mathrm{kJ/mol}$; the $\mathrm{N-O}$ bond enthalpy is $210\mathrm{kJ/mol}$; the $\mathrm{N=O}$ bond enthalpy is $630\mathrm{kJ/mol}$; the $\mathrm{N=N}$ bond enthalpy is $409\mathrm{kJ/mol}$; the $\mathrm{N\equiv N}$ bond enthalpy is $941\mathrm{kJ/mol}$; the $\mathrm{O-H}$ bond enthalpy is $463\mathrm{kJ/mol}$. (1) According to the absolute entropy value chart, calculate the total entropy change of this reaction ($\mathrm{J/mol\cdot K}$); (2) Calculate the total enthalpy change of this reaction ($\mathrm{kJ/mol}$).
ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: First describe the image: the absolute entropy value table in the attachment has two columns, the left column is Substance, and the right column is S°(J/mol·K). The standard entropies of the four gases in the table are: NH3(g)=193 J/(mol·K), N2O(g)=220 J/(mol·K), N2(g)=192 J/(mol·K), H2O(g)=189 J/(mol·K). Then reason: the reaction is 2NH3(g)+3N2O(g)→4N2(g)+3H2O(g). The entropy change is calculated as the total entropy of products minus the total entropy of reactants: ΔS°=[4S°(N2)+3S°(H2O)]−[2S°(NH3)+3S°(N2O)] = [4×192+3×189]−[2×193+3×220] = (768+567)−(386+660)=1335−1046=289 J/(mol·K). The enthalpy change is estimated according to bond enthalpies: bond breaking absorbs heat, bond formation releases heat, ΔH=total energy of bonds broken−total energy of bonds formed. In the reactants, 2NH3 contains 6 N-H; according to the N≡N–O structure of N2O, 3N2O contains 3 N≡N and 3 N-O. Total energy of bonds broken=6×388+3×941+3×210=2328+2823+630=5781 kJ. In the products, 4N2 contains 4 N≡N; 3H2O contains 6 O-H. Total energy of bonds formed=4×941+6×463=3764+2778=6542 kJ. Therefore ΔH=5781−6542=−761 kJ/mol reaction.

ready3_open_rewrite.resolved_question_text: Ammonia and nitrous oxide undergo the following reaction: $$2\mathrm{NH_3(g)} + 3\mathrm{N_2O(g)} \rightarrow 4\mathrm{N_2(g)} + 3\mathrm{H_2O(g)}$$ The enthalpy values of various bonds are known: the $\mathrm{N-H}$ bond enthalpy is $388\mathrm{kJ/mol}$; the $\mathrm{N-O}$ bond enthalpy is $210\mathrm{kJ/mol}$; the $\mathrm{N=O}$ bond enthalpy is $630\mathrm{kJ/mol}$; the $\mathrm{N=N}$ bond enthalpy is $409\mathrm{kJ/mol}$; the $\mathrm{N\equiv N}$ bond enthalpy is $941\mathrm{kJ/mol}$; the $\mathrm{O-H}$ bond enthalpy is $463\mathrm{kJ/mol}$. (1) According to the absolute entropy value chart, calculate the total entropy change of this reaction ($\mathrm{J/mol\cdot K}$); (2) Calculate the total enthalpy change of this reaction ($\mathrm{kJ/mol}$).
ready3_open_rewrite.final_cot: First describe the image: the absolute entropy value table in the attachment has two columns, the left column is Substance, and the right column is S°(J/mol·K). The standard entropies of the four gases in the table are: NH3(g)=193 J/(mol·K), N2O(g)=220 J/(mol·K), N2(g)=192 J/(mol·K), H2O(g)=189 J/(mol·K). Then reason: the reaction is 2NH3(g)+3N2O(g)→4N2(g)+3H2O(g). The entropy change is calculated as the total entropy of products minus the total entropy of reactants: ΔS°=[4S°(N2)+3S°(H2O)]−[2S°(NH3)+3S°(N2O)] = [4×192+3×189]−[2×193+3×220] = (768+567)−(386+660)=1335−1046=289 J/(mol·K). The enthalpy change is estimated according to bond enthalpies: bond breaking absorbs heat, bond formation releases heat, ΔH=total energy of bonds broken−total energy of bonds formed. In the reactants, 2NH3 contains 6 N-H; according to the N≡N–O structure of N2O, 3N2O contains 3 N≡N and 3 N-O. Total energy of bonds broken=6×388+3×941+3×210=2328+2823+630=5781 kJ. In the products, 4N2 contains 4 N≡N; 3H2O contains 6 O-H. Total energy of bonds formed=4×941+6×463=3764+2778=6542 kJ. Therefore ΔH=5781−6542=−761 kJ/mol reaction.
